content.user_title: Build Type-Safe React Apps with fp-ts
content.value_statement: React teams using fp-ts often struggle to connect functional types with hooks, forms, and async UI. This skill provides practical patterns for safer React and Next.js code.
actual_capabilities: Shows Option patterns for nullable React state.
Explains Either validation for form error handling.
Demonstrates TaskEither patterns for async data fetching.
Models loading, failure, and success with RemoteData.
Covers dependency injection and React 19 form patterns.
limitations: Does not install packages or modify projects by itself.
Examples assume TypeScript and basic fp-ts knowledge.
Does not replace official React or fp-ts documentation.
Does not audit production security or runtime behavior.

use_cases.title: Refactor Nullable State
use_cases.description: Replace null checks with Option so missing data is handled explicitly in React components.

use_cases.title: Improve Form Validation
use_cases.description: Use Either patterns to return useful validation errors without mixing invalid and valid states.

use_cases.title: Standardize Async UI
use_cases.description: Adopt TaskEither and RemoteData patterns for consistent loading, error, and success screens.

prompt_templates.title: Explain an fp-ts Type
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how to use Option in a React component with nullable user data. Keep the example practical and concise.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Form Validation
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this React form validation to use Either and collect all validation errors. Preserve the current user experience.

prompt_templates.title: Design Async State
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a TaskEither and RemoteData approach for this dashboard data flow. Include loading, retry, and error display behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Review React Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Next.js feature for fp-ts React patterns. Identify unsafe state, weak validation, and avoidable re-render risks.

output_examples.input: A profile component stores user data as null and checks it in several render branches.
output: The response recommends Option for the user state.
It explains how to render empty and loaded states clearly.
It notes where a simple default value is better than branching.

output_examples.input: A signup form stops after the first invalid field and gives unclear feedback.
output: The response recommends Either validation with accumulated errors.
It separates field validation from submit behavior.
It describes how users see all actionable errors at once.

output_examples.input: A dashboard has separate loading, data, and error booleans that can conflict.
output: The response recommends a RemoteData state model.
It describes the four allowed states and expected UI for each state.
It highlights how impossible state combinations are removed.

best_practices: Use Option when a value may be absent and the absence is expected.
Use Either or TaskEither when failures must be represented in the type system.
Keep React render state simple by modeling async workflows as explicit states.
anti_patterns: Do not wrap every value in fp-ts types when plain TypeScript is clearer.
Do not mix loading, data, and error booleans when those states can conflict.
Do not hide side effects inside render logic or validation functions.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it if you build React or Next.js applications with TypeScript and want practical fp-ts patterns.

faq.question: Does it require advanced functional programming knowledge?
faq.answer: No. The examples introduce Option, Either, TaskEither, and RemoteData through common React tasks.

faq.question: Can it help with React forms?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows how to validate forms and return useful error information with Either.

faq.question: Can it help with data fetching?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers TaskEither, custom fetch hooks, chained requests, parallel requests, and RemoteData states.

faq.question: Does it support React 19 patterns?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for use, useActionState, and useOptimistic in React 19 workflows.

faq.question: Will it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It is documentation guidance. Review any package installation command before running it in a project.
